title: David Dhawan Is Back. So Is the Kind of Bollywood Comedy NRIs Grew Up Rewinding on VHS Tapes.
excerpt: The trailer for 'Hai Jawani Toh Ishq Hona Hai' dropped today — Varun Dhawan, Mrunal Thakur, Pooja Hegde, a love triangle, two pregnancies, and a Chunnari Chunnari remake. The film hits theatres worldwide on June 5.
body:
There's a specific kind of Bollywood comedy that lives in the muscle memory of every NRI who grew up in the 90s and early 2000s. Loud. Colourful. Absurd. A hero caught between two women. A mother who doesn't know. A friend who makes everything worse. Govinda in a Hawaiian shirt.

David Dhawan invented that genre. And with the trailer for *Hai Jawani Toh Ishq Hona Hai*, released today, the 69-year-old director is betting it still works — this time with his son in the lead.

## The Trailer: What You're Getting

The three-minute, fifteen-second trailer opens in a courtroom. Varun Dhawan plays Jass, a married man desperate to become a father. Mrunal Thakur plays Baani, his wife, who's in court complaining to a judge that her husband won't stop pursuing her romantically. It's the kind of setup that sets the tone immediately: this is not a subtle film.

Cut to London. Jass meets Preet (Pooja Hegde) at a party and tells her he's "fully single." A romance ignites. Then Baani shows up at the door with news: she's pregnant. And then Preet shows up with the same news. Now Jass has to navigate two pregnancies, two women, and the complete implosion of his carefully constructed double life.

The trailer promises rapid-fire dialogue, slapstick set-pieces, and what appears to be a recreation of the iconic *Biwi No. 1* track "Chunnari Chunnari" — a callback that will land differently depending on whether you associate it with Salman Khan's original or your parents' DVD collection.

## The David Dhawan Factor

This is the fourth collaboration between David and Varun Dhawan, after *Main Tera Hero* (2014), *Judwaa 2* (2017), and the pandemic-era *Coolie No. 1* (2020). The track record is mixed — *Judwaa 2* was a genuine hit, *Coolie No. 1* was widely panned — but the David Dhawan brand has a floor that few Bollywood directors can match.

At the trailer launch event, David Dhawan got visibly emotional talking about working with his son. That moment — a veteran filmmaker who's directed Govinda, Salman Khan, and Anil Kapoor, getting teary over his kid — may be more emotionally interesting than anything in the film itself.

## The Cast Runs Deeper Than You Think

Beyond the three leads, the supporting cast reads like a deliberate nostalgia roster: Rakesh Bedi, Chunky Panday, Jimmy Shergill, Mouni Roy, Rajesh Kumar, and Ali Asgar. If you've watched any David Dhawan film, you know these are the character actors who make the chaos work.

The film is produced by Tips Films and co-produced by Maximilian Films (UK) — the British co-production arm signals confidence in international box office returns.

## Why This Matters for NRI Audiences

*Hai Jawani Toh Ishq Hona Hai* hits theatres worldwide on June 5, 2026. For diaspora audiences, the appeal is straightforward: this is comfort food cinema, deliberately engineered to remind you of the Bollywood your family watched together.

Whether that's a selling point or a warning sign depends on your tolerance for the genre. David Dhawan's best films — *Haseena Maan Jaayegi*, *Biwi No. 1*, the Govinda era — worked because they were unashamed of being silly. His worst films tried the same formula with less charm and more laziness.

The trailer suggests *Hai Jawani* is at least trying to earn its laughs. Varun Dhawan's physical comedy has improved markedly since *Coolie No. 1*, Mrunal Thakur brings genuine screen presence, and Pooja Hegde — fresh off the Telugu hit circuit — adds a different energy.

## The Legal Wrinkle

There's a side story worth noting: the trailer was briefly delayed due to a legal dispute over music rights. The details are still emerging, but it's been resolved enough for the trailer to drop today. Whether it affects the June 5 release date remains to be seen, but all signs currently point to an on-schedule launch.

## The Bottom Line

David Dhawan comedies are like IPL — you know exactly what you're getting, you've seen it before, and you'll still watch it because the format just works when the players show up. June 5. Theatres worldwide. You already know if this is for you.
nri_angle: Co-produced by Maximilian Films (UK), the film releases worldwide on June 5 with Day 1 international prints. For NRI millennials who grew up on David Dhawan's Govinda comedies, this is a nostalgia play aimed squarely at their demographic.
